newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lebed says NATO changes could sour views on arms.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says NATO changes could sour views on arms.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said on Monday that NATO eastward expansion could affect Russian attitudes to conventional forces and nuclear arms agreements already concluded.

Asked at a news conference if the plan could affect attitudes to agreements, especially in Russia's communist-dominated parliament, he replied: "This is the tragedy; that it could...The main thing is not to hurry (with NATO expansion plans). Then we will have success."
Lebed referred specifically to the START 2 agreement that drastically cuts nuclear arms arsenals in east and west and the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty.

Neither treaty has yet been formally ratified by Russia's parliament and opponents are rallying a majority in the lower house against ratification. The treaties are nonetheless being observed by all sides.
Lebed suggested that rights and obligations under the two treaties and other agreements on chemical weapons could be set out in a formal agreement signed before any NATO decision on expansion.
"It is a serious problem that must be solved comprehensively in a thorough and balanced way," he said.
